note: Pass with caveats. (1) LANGUAGE FALLBACK: Study 3 was run on 85 Italian participants and the paper states the 'same Italian version of the regulatory mode scale [21] used in Study 1' was administered. The Italian wording is published nowhere recoverable in scope: the deposit (S1 File .sav for this study is S3 File, doi 10.1371/journal.pone.0193357.s003, sha256 559ce822e2bbcf07c201f02fceae41db4d4fecf5a0cb204d87a9b148124c7429) was checked at BOTH label levels -- of 76 columns only 9 carry variable labels (serious/harmful/time/seriousRAT1/harmfulRAT1/seriousRAT2/harmfulRAT2/seriousrat_tot/harmfulrat_tot, none of them RMQ items), and the only value labels in the whole file are gender {0 men, 1 women}. The article's Supporting Information is exactly S1-S4 File, four .sav datasets, with no questionnaire; the Study 1 Measures section quotes one locomotion and one assessment item and quotes them in English. Base fields therefore hold English, language=Italian, no _translated columns: text_source=translated_substitute. (2) MAPPING: item codes loc1..loc12 (with locr6, locr9) ARE the .sav's own column names -- data/pierro_2018_selfforgiveness.py melts [c for c in d3.columns if c.lower().startswith('loc') and not c.lower().startswith('locomotion')] unrenamed, so no positional rename by the processing script is involved. But the .sav carries no labels for those columns, so the codes are bare positional indices into the RMQ Locomotion subscale and code->text is reconstructed, not read off a label. Reconstructed from the RMQ's own scoring key as distributed with the instrument form: Locomotion = [Q1 + Q3 + Q4 + Q5 + Q8 + (7-Q13) + Q16 + Q21 + (7-Q24) + Q25 + Q28 + Q29] / 12, which puts the two reverse-worded items at within-subscale positions 6 and 9 -- exactly where the codes carry their r marker (locr6, locr9). (3) ITEMS ARE STORED RAW HERE, AND THIS IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE SIBLING STUDY 1 TABLE. Reverse-coding status is a property of the table, not of the instrument, and it was checked rather than carried over: in pierro_2018_locomotion_s1 the stored columns are already reverse-recoded, whereas in this Study 3 file they are not. Evidence: the .sav's own 'locomotion' composite column equals the mean of the 12 columns WITH (7-x) applied to locr6 and locr9 to 0.000 max absolute difference over all 85 cases, and equals the plain unreversed mean nowhere (max abs diff 0.833); Cronbach's alpha after reversing those two is 0.8281 against the paper's published .83 for Study 3, while the stored direction gives 0.6488; and locr6/locr9 are the only two items with negative item-rest correlations in the stored direction (-0.249 and -0.470, against +0.209..+0.690 for the other ten). The shipped option anchors are therefore NOT flipped for locr6/locr9 -- resp 1 = Strongly Disagree for all twelve items, and a high resp on locr6/locr9 means the reverse-worded statement is TRUE of the respondent. (4) ANCHORS, ENDS ONLY. The paper states ratings were made on a 6-point Likert type scale 'with the response alternatives anchored at the ends with 1 (Strongly Disagree) to 6 (Strongly Agree)'. The RMQ form itself labels all six points (1 strongly disagree, 2 moderately disagree, 3 slightly disagree, 4 slightly agree, 5 moderately agree, 6 strongly agree), but the study's own description of what this sample saw outranks the instrument form, so option_text is populated for resp 1 and 6 only and left blank for 2-5 rather than guessed or padded with the level number. option_text capitalisation follows the paper ('Strongly Disagree'), not the instrument document's lowercase. (5) TRANSCRIPTION: item_text is verbatim from the RMQ instrument document including its typographic apostrophes and curly quotation marks; only the leading item numbering was stripped. instructions ships the document's first sentence verbatim; its second sentence ('Please respond according to the following scale:') and the six-point label block that follows were deliberately NOT shipped, because they describe the fully-labelled canonical administration and this study anchored only the ends. (6) STEP 3b: the live data is 12 items on a 1-6 scale with r markers at within-subscale positions 6 and 9, which is the Locomotion scale and not the 12-item Assessment scale administered alongside it in the same file (assr1/ass2../assr11/ass12, r markers at 1, 5 and 11), nor the 4-item 1-4 self-forgiveness scale, nor the two 10-item 1-5 PANAS scales. Three independent published quantities confirm the file is Study 3 and that the scale assignment is right: locomotion alpha .83 (computed .8281), assessment alpha .71 (computed .7136), and r(locomotion, assessment) = .12, p = .25 (computed .125). Table name and dictionary description are correct. (7) RIGHTS: ship. The Regulatory Mode Questionnaire already carries verdict=ship in itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv (registered 2026-09-10 from batch_137, which explicitly names pierro_2018_locomotion_s3 as queued under it); no fee, permission, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution term is stated on the DMIDI entry that distributes the form and scoring key, on the Kruglanski lab page, or on cuhigginslab.com/measures. Silence is permission. The register verdict was applied, not re-derived. (8) COVERAGE: all 12 items have all 85 respondents and the full 1-6 resp set is emitted per item, even though six items were never used at every level (loc3/loc4/loc7 observed 3-6, loc8/loc10/loc11 observed 2-6) -- those levels are in the table's overall resp set. RETRY TEST: not applicable, this is a clean pass, not a block.

Note that unlike the sibling table pierro_2018_locomotion_s1, the two reverse-worded items here are stored RAW, not already reverse-scored: the deposit's own locomotion composite is the mean with (7-x) applied to locr6 and locr9 (max difference 0.000 across all 85 cases), reversing them reproduces the paper's published alpha of .83 where the stored direction gives .65, and locr6 and locr9 are the only items with negative item-rest correlations as stored. So the anchors run the same way for all twelve items and a high response on locr6/locr9 means the reverse-worded statement is true of the respondent. Only the two end points of the 6-point scale are labelled, following the paper's own description of the administration; resp 2-5 carry no option text.

note: Pass with caveats. (1) INSTRUMENT / Step 3b: the live data is 4 items on a 1-4 scale, which is the 4-item state self-forgiveness measure Pierro et al. describe in Study 1 Measures ('4 items derived from the feeling subscale of Wohl and colleagues' State Self-Forgiveness Scale (SFS)'), NOT the Heartland Forgiveness Scale (that is the study's separate 6-item 1-7 Study 4 measure, pierro_2018_hfs_s4, blocked on instrument rights in batch_137) and not the 12-item 1-6 Locomotion/Assessment scales administered alongside it. Table name and dictionary Description are correct. (2) LANGUAGE FALLBACK: the scale was administered in Italian (323 Italian adults). The deposit (S1 File, the study's own SPSS .sav, sha256 2b5e55c9d153acaa41867af83f94c67bb9d686e4d8d50e81a664346ef1c32c9d) carries NO item wording at either label level: all 35 variable labels are None, and the only value labels in the file are gender {0 Men, 1 Women} and sample {0 students, 1 non-students}. No Italian item wording appears in the PLOS ONE article or any of its four supplements. Base fields therefore hold the ENGLISH wording the study's own paper prints, language=Italian, no _translated columns: text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied. (3) MAPPING: the IRW item codes ARE the .sav's own column names (data/pierro_2018_selfforgiveness.py selects sforgiveR1/sforgive2/sforgiveR3/sforgive4 and melts them unrenamed), so no positional rename is involved -- but the columns carry no labels, so code->text rests on the order the paper lists the four items in: 'I feel... rejecting of myself (Item Reversed, R), accepting of myself, dislike toward myself (R), forgiving myself'. The (R) markers fall at list positions 1 and 3, exactly where the codes carry their own R marker. mapping_basis=paper_order. (4) ITEMS ARE STORED ALREADY REVERSE-SCORED. Cronbach's alpha on the stored directions is 0.717, matching the paper's published .72 for the total sample, while un-reversing sforgiveR1/sforgiveR3 collapses it to -0.613; all four items have positive corrected item-total r as stored (+0.587/+0.502/+0.537/+0.408); and the .sav's own 'selfforgive' composite equals the plain unweighted mean of the four stored columns to 0.000 over 323 cases (the reverse-recoded mean misses it by up to 1.5). The shipped anchors for sforgiveR1 and sforgiveR3 are therefore FLIPPED (resp 1 = Completely, resp 4 = Not at all), following the burkert_2019_whoqol_bref precedent; this is an override of the printed anchor direction and is disclosed here and in public_note. (5) ANCHORS, ENDS ONLY: the paper states ratings were made 'on a 4-point scale with the response alternatives anchored at the ends with 1 (Not at all) to 4 (Completely)', so option_text is populated for resp 1 and 4 only and left blank for 2 and 3 rather than padded with the level number. (6) NO INSTRUCTIONS SHIPPED: the paper describes the induction procedure in third-person prose ('participants were told to think of the most significant experience in which they did something they believe to have been wrong') and quotes only the fragment 'right now'; no verbatim instruction text is published, so 'instructions' is left blank rather than filled with an IRW paraphrase. (7) RIGHTS: no restriction locatable on the State Self-Forgiveness Scale. Checked the originator's own pages -- carleton.ca/psychology/people/michael-j-a-wohl/ and carleton.ca/bettermentlabs/ (both fetched 2026-09-10, HTTP 200) -- which host no instrument-distribution page and state no fee, permission requirement, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution term; web search for terms on the SSFS returned only the CJBS article notice. Under irw#1945 as restated 2026-09-08, silence is permission and a bare journal copyright notice is a notice about the article, not a term governing the instrument. Note separately that the wording actually shipped is Pierro et al.'s own English rendering of their 4-item Italian adaptation, printed in a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE article, not verbatim SSFS wording. The HFS block registered in batch_137 does NOT reach this table: different instrument, different study. (8) COVERAGE: all four items use all four resp levels in the source .sav (min 1, max 4 for each), so every item has an option row for every level its own respondents used.
